location: docs/mvp0/PRODUCT-PLAN.md section 14, paragraph 'Cost when the free pools are gone'
claim: 100 edits and 5 blueprints on Sonnet 5 cost about ₹120 of a ₹299 month at list price
evidence: Plan's own token counts: edit 4,000 in / 800 out; blueprint 60,000 in / 23,000 out. Sonnet 5 list $2 in / $10 out per MTok (section 14 table and r1 report). Edit = 4,000 x 2 / 1e6 + 800 x 10 / 1e6 = $0.008 + $0.008 = $0.016; 100 edits = $1.60. Blueprint = 60,000 x 2 / 1e6 + 23,000 x 10 / 1e6 = $0.12 + $0.23 = $0.35; 5 blueprints = $1.75. Total $3.35 x 95.96 = ₹321.47, not ₹120. On Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5): 100 x 0.008 + 5 x 0.175 = $1.675 = ₹160.7. With 50 percent batch on Sonnet: ₹160.7. Plan v3 section 9 had computed the same caps at 'about ₹305 on Sonnet against ₹246 net'.
impact: A fully active Pro user costs more in model fees (₹321) than the gross price (₹299) and far more than the net after GST and Razorpay (about ₹246). Pro at the stated caps loses money on Sonnet 5 at list price; the plan reports the opposite. Every Pro margin and break-even statement built on ₹120 is wrong.
fix: Re-derive the Pro model cost with the working shown; either route Pro edits to Haiku with Sonnet reserved for blueprints (about ₹160), cut the Pro caps, raise the price, or state that caching and batch are required for margin and measure them in week one. Restore v3's honest sentence.
source: docs/mvp0/PRODUCT-PLAN.md section 14; docs/mvp0/MVP0-PLAN-v3.md section 9; verify/2026-09-17/research/2026-09-17-r1-free-llm.md section E

location: docs/mvp0/PRODUCT-PLAN.md section 14 'The routing'; S01 fine print 'We never train on your documents'
claim: Never in the chain: ... anything whose terms were not opened
evidence: The routing sends edits and blueprints to 'OpenRouter's Nvidia-served free endpoints'. The r1 report: 'NVIDIA build.nvidia.com ... Not stated on opened pages' for training, and for OpenRouter free endpoints 'Depends on the endpoint's provider'. UPGRADED 2026-09-17 on live evidence from the AI provider verification worker: OpenRouter's model endpoint metadata for the Nvidia-served free endpoints carries training true and retainsPrompts true, and the NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service that OpenRouter names as governing that endpoint state that NVIDIA collects User Content and Generated Content to improve NVIDIA products and services, including AI models. location: docs/mvp0/screens/s15-blueprint-ready.html kickoff prompt; docs/mvp0/screens/s18-public-view.html; docs/mvp0/PRODUCT-PLAN.md S15
claim: 1. mkdir -p docs/kit && curl -sL .../v1/kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C docs/kit  2. cd docs/kit && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS (stop if any line fails)
evidence: The checksum file travels inside the tarball it is asked to verify, and the check runs after extraction. It detects a corrupted transfer, not a substituted kit: anyone who can replace the tarball can replace SHA256SUMS in it. The prompt also tells an agent to fetch and unpack an archive from a URL before any human has looked at it, into the agent's working repository, which is the fetch-then-execute pattern the plan's own security section warns about.
impact: The kickoff prompt teaches every user's agent an unsafe habit and gives a false assurance ('stop if any line fails'). A poisoned kit at a look-alike link would pass the check.
fix: Publish the kit's root hash out of band (on the published page and in the prompt itself), have the prompt verify the tarball against that hash before extraction, and tell the agent to read before it builds. Consider signed manifests when the MCP server ships.

location: docs/mvp0/screens/s20-review.html; docs/mvp0/screens/s07-ai-edit.html
claim: Accept, Reject, Reply, Accept all ... nothing is applied without a click
evidence: On S20 Accept is the filled primary button, Reject the outlined secondary, and 'Accept all three' applies a person's edit, an AI edit and an agent's edit in one click. The research the plan cites (2026-09-16-note-research.md section C) says people over-accept AI suggestions and that the designs which cut over-reliance were the least liked. The plan's rule (section 3.5 of the print sheet) is 'every AI edit needs an explicit accept', which one bulk button satisfies in letter only.
impact: The review queue, the plan's only gate between an agent and a file, is designed to be cleared fastest by accepting everything. That is the automation-bias failure the plan says it guards against.
fix: Make Accept and Reject equal-weight buttons, remove Accept all for AI and agent items (keep it for a named person's edits), and show the diff inline before Accept is enabled on agent items.

location: docs/mvp0/PRODUCT-PLAN.md section 18 Phase D (published pages) against docs/mvp0/MVP0-PLAN-v3.md section 15
claim: Phase D ships 'published pages with the .md twin' and the plan mentions no grievance apparatus, takedown path or moderation anywhere
evidence: IT Rules 2021 rule 3(2)(a), opened 2026-09-17 from the MeitY PDF: an intermediary 'shall prominently publish ... the name of the Grievance Officer and his contact details as well as mechanism by which a user or a victim may make complaint', acknowledge within twenty-four hours and resolve within fifteen days, with a 72-hour path for removal requests; rule 3(1)(d): removal 'in no case later than thirty-six hours' after a court or government order. v3 costed the apparatus at 74 founder-hours in Phase A 'before the first stranger publishes'. v4 contains zero occurrences of takedown, moderation or grievance. This row is a component of blocker F008.
impact: Hosting strangers' pages at frontmatter.in/p/slug makes the company an intermediary; without the rule 3(2) apparatus the section 79 safe harbour is lost, which is personal liability for what a stranger publishes, not a fine.
fix: Restore v3's Phase A row into Phase D and gate the published-page launch on it: a named Grievance Officer with a published address, a report link on every public page (S18), 24-hour acknowledgement, the 15-day and 72-hour clocks, a 36-hour court-order path, and a preservation log. One risk row, one founder question.

location: docs/mvp0/PRODUCT-PLAN.md sections 1 and 13; S01
claim: You sign in with Google or GitHub and land on your documents (implicit: anyone may)
evidence: The plan has zero hits for age, children, parental or under 18 in 659 lines. DPDP Act 2023 section 9 requires verifiable parental consent before processing a child's personal data (a child is under eighteen) and bars tracking or targeted advertising at children; commencement of the section is by notification and the rules' dates could not be opened (egazette refused connection).
